Energy in, energy out
Athletes need more energy on training days than rest days. Not eating enough can leave you tired and slow recovery.
This tool maps rest to moderately active and training to active levels in the 2020–2025 tables. Real plans are personalized.
Carbohydrate
Carbohydrate is the main fuel for hard exercise. Foods the day before and day of a game fill stores.
Model wake tank: 30 plus up to 50, from previous-day carbohydrate grams divided by 8.
Before
Eat 1 to 4 hours before: mostly carbohydrate, some protein, less fat and fiber so it sits well.
Model meals add carbohydrate grams times 0.25 over 60 minutes. During drinks spread their contribution over play.
After
Carbohydrate and protein after hard exercise help refuel and repair muscles.
Tool threshold: one meal within 2 hours, with at least 40 g carbohydrate and 15 g protein.
Fluids
Drink before, during and after, more in heat. Water is the main drink; sports drinks can help in long, hard sessions.
Drink checks record presence, not amounts. Awake model drain: 0.05 per minute. Play drains differ by sport.
Supplements
Most teens can get what they need from food. Supplements are not checked by the FDA for safety or effectiveness before sale.
Tank outcomes are model thresholds: 30 percent or more is Strong finish; 15 to below 30 is Running low late.
